Subject: MSA: defining proof thresholds for intentional misconduct (redline attached)

Team — attaching an updated MSA redline focused on the exclusions to the liability cap for intentional misconduct / fraud. Nimbus asked us to clarify the scope, the burden of proof, and any materiality threshold so their procurement/legal team can sign off without needing to escalate to their GC.

High-level items I tried to capture in the draft: 
- Clear carve-out language for proven fraud and for willful misconduct (intentional acts). 
- A separate, narrower pathway for reckless conduct (we propose objective gates rather than automatic exclusion). 
- Burden of proof recommendation (I put in "clear and convincing evidence" but flagged for discussion).
- A materiality floor for certain exclusions so we avoid open-ended exposure on trivial incidents.

Attachments: MSA_redline_rk_v2.docx (redline); evidence-gating-proposal.pdf (workflow for investigations).

Thanks Rachel — looked through the draft. A few substantive edits and rationale below (I also embedded them in the DOCX):

1) Carve-out structure:
- Proposed language: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the liability cap set forth in Section X shall not apply to (a) proven fraudulent acts, (b) proven intentional wrongdoing or willful misconduct, or (c) third-party claims to the extent caused by fraud or willful misconduct."

2) Burden of proof: 
- Recommend "clear and convincing evidence" for fraud/willful misconduct. It protects the company from speculative allegations while remaining a recognized evidentiary standard. I flagged an alternative ("preponderance") if sales thinks Nimbus will push back hard.

3) Materiality / floor: 
- To avoid unlimited exposure for minor issues, add a materiality gate: "For the purposes of subparagraph (c) above, the exclusion shall only apply to Claims resulting in direct damages in excess of $250,000 or 5% of the Order Form value, whichever is lower." 
- Rationale: keeps carve-out meaningful to the customer while capping trivial disputes.

4) Recklessness vs. gross negligence: 
- I propose a separate, narrower exclusion for conduct that meets a defined "reckless" standard. Recklessness should require (i) conscious disregard of a known substantial risk and (ii) a causal link to the damages. Recklessness exclusion should also require objective corroboration (see evidence-gating).

5) Evidence gating / investigation: 
- Insert a 30-day preliminary review period where either party can submit prima facie evidence. If prima facie threshold met, the parties will either agree on an independent investigator or engage a mutually agreed external counsel to adjudicate within 90 days. That procedure limits frivolous claims and gives us time to contain incidents operationally.

Commercial note (Dev) — the materiality numbers are negotiable, but anything that eliminates the cap without a clear floor will materially affect pricing and approval thresholds.

I left the consequential damages carve-out untouched for now (we already have the standard carve-out for indemnified third-party IP claims).

Lauren

Appreciate the draft and the materiality suggestion — good move to have a floor. From commercial POV a couple of points: 

- $250k / 5% is a reasonable place to start for enterprise customers but we should calibrate to ACV for smaller deals. For Nimbus (initial order ~ $1.2M ARR), the proposed floor is fine.
- Big ask from procurement will be to narrow the independent investigator mechanism. Nimbus will prefer to rely on internal findings or their external counsel (and may resist a third-party investigator). Compromise: require prima facie evidence and then allow either party to request independent review — cost-shifting to the losing party. That reduces frivolous claims and discourages fishing expeditions.
- On burden of proof: "clear and convincing" is legally defensible but customers often push for "preponderance". If we give ground on burden of proof, we should tighten the materiality floor and keep the evidence gating.
- Consequential damages carve-out: keep as-is. Do not expand to cover indirect lost profits unless tied to fraud that is proven under the agreed standard.

Operational constraint for Markus: if we accept an independent investigator route, we need at least 10 business days notice and a dedicated point-of-contact for evidence collection.

I'll loop in Sales Ops to confirm whether we need an approval from Revenue Ops for exceptions under $X.

—Dev
